items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: You know, Grieg. So it was like, and there was this piece they were doing...

ctx.x: Right. Well the whole thing with the Trans-Siberian Orchestra had this sort of path from the heavy metal band into this Christmas-oriented — I guess it’s a seasonal —

Well it started off seasonal but it’s become kind of a year-round thing. That — again I was doing session work and I had left Record Plant but, you know, all my connections I’d made there were still there. Paul O’Neill, who was the main guy in TSO, was doing his first record with a band called Savatage, which is the metal band that TSO kind of spun off of. You know, the same creative core went and formed Trans-Siberian Orchestra. And this was in the mid-80’s. They were doing “Hall of the Mountain King.” And I got…

this piece they were doing that was kind of war between the rock band and the orchestra. So basically I went and played every single part one at a time, of the orchestra, but it was a more in-your-face type of sound because it was a keyboard thing. But it also had a realism to it because if there was five string lines I’d play it with five different sounds and layer it all together. So you could have done it with people, but I was there, and I just did it, and it was a way of making it really tight-sounding. So…
